HR@10 against 99 sampled negatives measures success within that candidate set; it does not establish full-catalog ranking quality. Sampled metrics can even reverse model ordering in expectation ([Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)). Fixed users/candidates support paired comparisons, but leave uncertainty across candidate samples unmeasured. With 200 users/category, one additional hit changes category HR by 0.5 percentage points and four-category macro HR by 0.125 points. Repeatedly choosing architectures/checkpoints on these same outcomes creates selection optimism; a fixed evaluation seed does not prevent validation overfitting ([Cawley–Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)).

Recommended analysis: retain each model’s binary hit outcome for every identical user/candidate set. Define paired differences d=h_candidate−h_baseline; report Δ=(1/4)Σ_category mean(d). Construct a 95% stratified paired-bootstrap interval by resampling 200 user pairs within each category, preserving pairing and recomputing the equal-weight macro difference ([paired bootstrap](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html)). A paired permutation test swaps model labels within user pairs and recomputes Δ under exchangeability ([permutation documentation](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.permutation_test.html?highlight=difference)). Report category win/loss discordances; exact McNemar tests use those discordances, with multiplicity adjustment if making four category-level claims ([McNemar documentation](https://www.statsmodels.org/dev/generated/statsmodels.stats.contingency_tables.mcnemar.html)).

Keep macro validation HR@10 as the sole selection metric; intervals, discordances and tests describe evidence rather than introduce another objective. These analyses assume independent users and concern the four fixed datasets and fitted models; they omit retraining variability and do not correct adaptive search bias. Log all comparisons, predeclare confirmatory contrasts where possible, and treat winner-on-validation significance as exploratory until the host’s separate held-out evaluation.
